L01.note: Three translation-quality terms (literal/idiomatic/faithful) with exacting as the outlier; faithful is the balanced one between the literal/idiomatic poles.

L04.note: muted is the hedged middle among undetectable/exaggerated extremes.

L07.note: noise is the one option without an article; instrument-data register fits it.

L08.note: elegant is the classic secondary academic sense (of a solution) among plain descriptors.

L10.note: Dictionary senses of 'color'; the figurative sense is the one an academic passage would test.

L13.note: calculate is the non-sensory odd one out, weak signal.

L14.note: Senses of 'economy'; the abstract 'sparing use of means' is the academic sense.

L17.note: Senses of 'temperate'; 'moderate and restrained' is the figurative sense used of people or arguments.

L19.note: suspended is the hedged middle among destroyed/reversed.

L20.note: Senses of 'economy' as a noun; spareness is the aesthetic sense typical of an arts passage.

L25.note: Senses of 'homely'; plain and unadorned is the secondary sense a passage would test.

L28.note: Sense set for a word like accretions/increments; the gradual-accumulation sense is the academic one against financial and decorative traps.

L29.note: Senses of 'address'; the unfamiliar 'skill in handling situations' sense is the one worth testing.

L32.note: Senses of 'temperate' again; measured is the figurative sense.

L35.note: coarse in its resolution/granularity sense is the polysemous academic member of the set.

L37.note: conservative in the estimate sense is the polysemous academic member of the set.
